words.sense: A public written declaration of goals, beliefs, and proposed actions.
misconceptions: A list of positions is not necessarily a public declaration.

words.sense: The set of policies and positions a political group supports.
misconceptions: Public statements can describe but are not identical to the policy set.

semantic_axes.description: Communication document versus the collection of supported policy commitments.

edges.boundary_rule: A manifesto is the public declaration itself; a platform is the bundle of policies or positions a group stands for.

misconceptions.M1: Confuses a public programmatic text with the policies that it communicates.
misconceptions.M2: Treats endorsed positions as though they must be a published document.
misconceptions.M3: Assumes the existence of campaign material changes what the named subject is.

chains.frame: Which word best describes Samira’s campaign document?

beats.text: Samira posts a signed letter announcing why her student movement exists, what it believes, and what it plans to change.
beats.decisive_clue: a signed public statement lays out beliefs and aims
beats.reason: The first detail establishes a signed public statement lays out beliefs and aims; that is the meaningful distinction.

beats.text: She asks every candidate to share the same letter publicly before campaigning begins.
beats.decisive_clue: the letter serves as a shared public announcement of the movement
beats.reason: The new detail confirms the letter serves as a shared public announcement of the movement and rules out the competing sense.

chains.feedback_short: The letter is a public statement of the movement’s beliefs and plans.
chains.feedback_deep: Manifesto means public statement of beliefs and plans. Platform means collection of supported policies. Here, the subject is the published declaration, not merely its underlying policies.
chains.contrast_rule: A manifesto tells the public; a platform is what the group stands for.

hints.attention: Is the subject a communication or a set of positions?
hints.axis: Communication document versus the collection of supported policy commitments.
hints.contrast: A manifesto tells the public; a platform is what the group stands for.

beats.reason: The first detail establishes an elected group adopts three policy positions; that is the meaningful distinction.

beats.reason: The new detail confirms support for the set persists independently of meeting timing and rules out the competing sense.

chains.feedback_short: Three supported measures form an agenda; the meeting date changes nothing.
chains.feedback_deep: Manifesto means public statement of beliefs and plans. Platform means collection of supported policies. Here, the central subject is the program of positions, not a written statement launching the campaign.
